title: Invoice slice mapping guidelines: ambiguous tag resolution and UX decisions
body:
Purpose
This note captures UX decisions and mapping rules for invoice "slices" (aka CSV/JSON exports used by customers to allocate cost to tags/centers). Focus: how the console resolves ambiguous or conflicting tags during export and how we surface that to customers in the UI (warnings, preview, auto-resolve).

Context / problem
- Customers upload/export invoices and expect deterministic mapping from token-level usage to cost centers (tags, cost-centers, projects).
- In practice customers have overlapping tag sources (manual tagging in console, CSV-provided tags, default workspace tags, external billing IDs). When multiple sources provide different values for the same line, exported slices can be ambiguous.
- We currently have a minimal precedence rule (CSV override console), but customers report surprising allocations and need better tools to preview, reconcile, and opt into a chosen resolution.

Goals
1) Make resolution deterministic and discoverable.
2) Give customers an easy preview of how slices will be generated before download.
3) Offer explicit conflict UI and safe defaults (no silent surprises).
4) Keep export UX lightweight for simple cases; surface advanced controls progressively.

Assumptions
- Most customers will not want to configure complex rules — default heuristics should work for 80% cases.
- Power users need rule overrides and preserve auditability.

Resolution rules (proposal)
- Source priority (default, high->low): 1) Explicit mapping rows in CSV export-props column with "_allocation_tag" (highest precedence), 2) Console-level resource tags (per-model/per-route), 3) Workspace default tags, 4) Billing connector-derived mapping (lowest).
- If multiple values exist at same precedence level, treat as a within-row conflict (see conflict handling below).
- If no tag present, class as "unmapped" and place in a special bucket called _Unallocated (customer can remap post-export).

Conflict handling (UX + rules)
- Detect conflicts at export-preview time (before download).
- Present conflict types: "row-level mismatch" (CSV shows tag A, console shows tag B for same resource), "multi-tag present" (single resource has two different console tags), and "missing primary key" (no stable identifier to join).
- For each conflicting row show: resource id, timestamp range, proposed resolved tag (based on priority), alternate candidates (with source labels), and a suggested action (accept, force CSV override, mark as review).
- Default suggested action: accept resolution by priority and add a soft warning. If the dataset has >1% rows in conflict, pre-check a modal that requires confirmation.

Preview panel wireframe notes
- Place a lightweight preview above the Download button showing three numbers: Total rows, Rows with conflicts, Rows Unmapped.
- Inline small table (paginated) with sample 10 conflicts and a "View more" that opens full conflict modal. Columns: Timestamp, Resource id, Raw CSV tag, Console tag, Resolved tag, Action selector (Accept / Replace with CSV / Mark for review).
- Action selectors should be dropdowns with keyboard accessible options and quick keyboard shortcuts: A = accept, C = use CSV, R = mark review.
- Provide an export-simulation toggle: "Show costs by tag after resolution" which calculates expected spend distribution (approx) so finance can validate.

Microcopy and error states
- Conflict banner copy: "We found N potential mapping conflicts in this export. We applied our default resolution rules, but please preview to confirm allocations before downloading."
- Unmapped rows tooltip: "Rows without an assignment will be labeled _Unallocated in the export CSV. You can map these post-download or update your mapping rules."
- When >5% unmapped: show inline tip: "Consider adding a workspace default tag or including _allocation_tag column in your CSV to reduce unmapped lines."
- If no primary key present in imported CSV: inline error (blocking): "CSV is missing a stable resource identifier (model_id or route_id). Add a unique id column or enable fuzzy matching in advanced options."

Advanced options (collapsed by default)
- Rule editor (power users): define per-column precedence, regex-based tag remap (e.g., /^eng-.*/ -> Engineering), and date-window overrides (useful for cost center reorganizations).
- Enable fuzzy-matching: attempts to join CSV rows to console resources using name similarity (threshold slider). Warning: fuzzy matches are best-effort and will be labeled in output.
- Batch-apply corrections: customers can select a set of conflict rows and apply a bulk mapping (e.g., set 234 rows to "Customer A").

Export CSV schema changes (compatibility notes)
- Add audit columns: resolved_tag_source (one of csv|console|workspace|connector|fuzzy), resolved_at (ISO timestamp), conflict_flag (true/false), original_tag_candidates (semicolon-separated list).
- Preserve existing column names for backward compatibility; only append new audit columns. Document in release notes.

Accessibility and keyboard flows
- Conflict modal must be navigable via keyboard with clear focus on first actionable element (Accept/Use CSV).
- Provide ARIA live region updates when bulk actions complete ("Mapped 120 rows to Engineering").

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Default priority rules implemented server-side and applied at preview time.
- Preview panel shows counts and sample table.
- Conflict modal allows accepting default resolution or replacing with CSV value per-row and supports bulk apply.
- Exported CSV includes the new audit columns.
- UX copy and warnings in place.

Metrics to validate success
- % of exports with >0 conflicts reduced (or at least awareness increased via previews).
- Reduction in support tickets referencing "incorrect allocation" for accounts with preview enabled.
- NPS feedback from billing admins in pilot group.

Edge cases and notes for engineering
- Large exports (10M rows): preview must be sampled. Sampling strategy: top 10 conflicts by spend, then random 90 rows.
- Do not compute fuzzy matching by default for scaled exports unless customer toggles on.
- Keep audit columns small — original_tag_candidates truncated to 1024 chars.

Backlog / prioritization (rough)
- P0: Priority rules + export audit columns + server-side preview counts (3 sprints)
- P1: Conflict modal + per-row actions + keyboard accessibility (2 sprints)
- P2: Advanced rule editor + fuzzy matching + bulk corrections (2–3 sprints)

Open questions
- Should we allow customers to save a set of rule presets at org level? (likely yes; will require meta storage and UI to manage).
- Do we auto-apply previously-saved presets on subsequent exports? (opt-in toggle needed).
- How do we reflect changes retroactively for historical invoices? Provide a "re-run mapping" job? (costly; needs infra gating).

Next steps
- Product meet on 2024-10-07 to finalize wording and acceptance criteria (owners: Aisha, Marcus).
- PM to create JIRA epic JIRA-INV-400 capturing P0 tasks and link to Confluence spec.
- SRE/infra to scope preview sampling cost for large exports.

Notes for design pairing (Sofia)
- Explore a subtle left-border color for conflict rows (amber) and use inline chips to show the resolved source (e.g., "resolved: console").
- Prototype a compact conflict modal that supports keyboard batch-selection with shift+click.

Appendix: sample CSV row mapping examples (for internal QA)
- CSV row example 1 (explicit CSV tag): resource_id=route-123, timestamp=2024-08-15T12:00Z, _allocation_tag=MobileTeam -> resolved_tag=MobileTeam, resolved_tag_source=csv
- CSV row example 2 (console vs CSV mismatch): resource_id=model-77, timestamp=2024-08-20T00:00Z, csv_tag=Infra, console_tag=Platform -> using default priority resolved_tag=Platform, show conflict with option to Replace with CSV
- CSV row example 3 (no id, fuzzy match): resource_name="search-main", csv_tag=Search -> fuzzy matches model-99 with score 0.82 -> resolved_tag=Search, resolved_tag_source=fuzzy (labeled in CSV)

Owner and contacts
- Primary: Aisha Patel (PM)
- Design: Sofia Ramirez
- Eng lead: Marcus Li
- Billing SME: Evan Brooks

End of doc
